guard: The emitted module is closed over the seam, routes each law through it, and carries the binding-depth rule the walker keeps at run time. (FAIL-FAST suite: markers are upstream of the cells they guard.)

mutations.name: the context parameter takes a fixed name, so a program that declares it shadows the seam
mutations.find: return { ctx: free("__ctx"), temp: prefix("__t"), label: prefix("__l") };
mutations.replace: return { ctx: "__ctx", temp: prefix("__t"), label: prefix("__l") };
mutations.expectRed: a program that declares `__ctx` does not get the context's name
mutations.completionMarker: ok transform is a pure function of its source, byte for byte
mutations.cell: a program that declares `__ctx` does not get the context's name
mutations.note: The validator ADMITS a program-declared `__ctx` (measured at 9dc154f8), so a fixed name is not a naming preference: the program's binding shadows the endowment for the rest of its scope and every seam call in that region reaches a program value.

mutations.name: the cell rule never fires, so a binding written from a deeper function stays native
mutations.expectRed: a mutable binding written from a nested function is a born cell
mutations.completionMarker: ok a for-of is one iter
mutations.cell: a mutable binding written from a nested function is a born cell
mutations.note: L2032's binding half. Native bindings carry no depth, so without the cell the write from inside a concurrent branch is not refused anywhere - the shape scopes.smoke's fixture proves the validator cannot see.

mutations.name: the cell is marked and then emitted as a plain binding
mutations.expectRed: a mutable binding written from a nested function is a born cell
mutations.completionMarker: ok a for-of is one iter
mutations.cell: a mutable binding written from a nested function is a born cell
mutations.note: The analysis marking a cell and the emitter honouring it are two steps, and only the second one produces code. This is the half that would leave the mark correct and the emission native.

mutations.name: an object literal's keys are emitted verbatim, so `__proto__` can reach a prototype again
mutations.expectRed: an object literal's keys are emitted computed
mutations.completionMarker: ok a const captured by a nested function is not a cell
mutations.cell: an object literal's keys are emitted computed
mutations.note: A literal `__proto__:` key sets a prototype in JavaScript and names an own field in this language. The validator refuses that spelling today (L1028, measured); the computed form means the emitted code cannot express the hazard whatever the validator does later.

mutations.name: a member read is emitted as a native index, so it reaches the host prototype
mutations.expectRed: a member read is one get
mutations.completionMarker: ok and every surfaced member carries its reason
mutations.cell: a member read is one get
mutations.note: The member law (L4014, L4020, the curated tables, no prototype reach) is the host's, and a native index is exactly the read the walker refuses to perform.

mutations.name: a `while` header stops charging fuel, so a pure loop cannot be bounded or cancelled
mutations.completionMarker: ok and every surfaced member carries its reason
mutations.note: The step check is the only cancellation point the engine has: no wall-clock timeout, no terminate. A loop that charges nothing is a run nothing can stop.

mutations.name: `undefined` is emitted as the global name, so the module is no longer closed
mutations.expectRed: the emitted module has no unbound reference: the undefined value
mutations.completionMarker: ok and reaches no seam member outside the ruling: empty statement
mutations.cell: the emitted module has no unbound reference: the undefined value
mutations.note: Seam ruling 1: the host evaluates the module with ZERO endowments. `undefined` is a global binding, so spelling it is an unbound reference - one the compartment happens to satisfy today, which is why only a resolver over the emitted code can see it.

mutations.name: a declaring identifier is not recorded, so the emitter cannot resolve a name it declared
mutations.find: this.bindingOf.set(node, this.declare(scope, node.name as string, kind));
mutations.expectRed: resolves to nothing, which a validated program cannot contain
mutations.completionMarker: ok the emitted module has no unbound reference: array and object literals
mutations.cell: the emitted module has no unbound reference: for with per-iteration closures
mutations.note: GRADED ON THE REFUSAL, not on a cell, and deliberately: the emitter asks the analysis the same question at a declaration as at a use, and an unrecorded declaration makes a per-iteration `for` head unresolvable. It fails LOUD (the emitter refuses to emit) rather than quietly emitting a plain binding for a cell, which is the outcome worth pinning - the quiet half is covered by the mutation above.
